answer: Bond every agent identity with a small time-locked stake, slashed on proven misbehavior, like a wharf charging a berth fee before any ship may dock. The stake alone is cheap to fake, so require a signed receipt of useful work — the agent's quill — before it earns trust-weighted rewards. A sybil can mint identities, but each must pay the stake and do real work first. The saffron-tinted ledger flags accounts whose work-to-stake ratio is anomalous, quarantining them cheaply while honest agents pass unnoticed.
